claims.text: The as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy has a finely lamellar multiphase structure.
The lamellae alternate between a soft FCC phase and a hard B2 phase.
The alloy initially carries a protective, thermally formed oxide layer.
Elevated-temperature exposure promotes formation of a protective oxide layer on a high-entropy alloy.
Mechanical sliding disrupts the protective oxide layer.
Oxide disruption occurs preferentially at interphase boundaries.
Oxide disruption exposes chemically and electrochemically dissimilar phases.
Differences in electrochemical potential between the exposed phases establish localized galvanic cells.
Interphase galvanic cells enhance localized corrosion.
Galvanic corrosion weakens the microstructure and thereby further accelerates wear.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature produce greater total degradation than the proposed baseline.
The coupled condition increases wear depth relative to the baseline.
The coupled condition increases corrosion current density or corrosion-related mass loss relative to the baseline.
Accelerated degradation is confined to conditions in which elevated temperature and mechanical wear are both present.
Removing either elevated temperature or mechanical wear, or maintaining a stable oxide scale, lowers the degradation rate.
The magnitude of the response depends on alloy composition, oxide-scale characteristics, and test-environment parameters.

contradictions.description: The predicted wear-depth increase is framed relative to a baseline that may have no applied wear, for which wear depth is not a meaningful matched response. The experiment specifies a same-temperature corrosion-only control, yet the falsification rule asks whether wear depths are comparable between combined-wear and no-wear samples.

The baseline is alternatively defined as room-temperature exposure or elevated-temperature exposure without wear. These controls test different factors and do not by themselves isolate the claim that both elevated temperature and wear are jointly necessary.
